posts.title: Ransomware Attack on Oklahoma Medical Center Impacts 133,000
posts.author: Admin
posts.excerpt: Great Plains Regional Medical Center in Oklahoma is notifying over 133,000 individuals that their personal information was compromised in a ransomware incident.
paragraphs: Great Plains Regional Medical Center in Oklahoma is notifying over 133,000 individuals that their personal information was compromised in a ransomware incident affecting systems used for patient care and administration.

Organisations in healthcare remain high-value targets because downtime directly affects patient services. Incidents like this underline the need for tested backups, segmented networks, and response plans that legal and communications teams can execute quickly.
Fencesense helps teams translate public advisories into patch priorities, monitoring changes, and tabletop exercises so leadership knows what to do when a vendor or sector peer is hit.

posts.title: Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)
posts.author: Admin
posts.excerpt: Cloud Workload Protection is how organisations safeguard applications, virtual machines, containers, and serverless functions running in the cloud.
paragraphs: Cloud Workload Protection (CWP) is a security approach designed to safeguard cloud-hosted workloads, such as applications, virtual machines, containers, and serverless functions, from potential cyber threats.

As organisations adopt cloud environments, CWP becomes part of keeping visibility, control, and protection over infrastructure that moves and scales. Without it, new workloads appear faster than the team can review them.
Fencesense helps teams put workload protection next to architecture and operations, so coverage follows the estate instead of lagging a quarter behind it.

posts.title: CrowdStrike CNAPP
posts.author: Admin
posts.excerpt: CrowdStrike's Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform brings workload protection, visibility, and compliance into one view of cloud-native applications.
paragraphs: CrowdStrike's Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) is a security platform for cloud-native applications across their lifecycle. It brings several security functions into one place so teams are not stitching together a separate tool for every question.
A unified platform pulls workload protection, vulnerability management, and compliance monitoring together. That reduces the overhead of running many consoles that do not share context.

Visibility extends across cloud workloads, containers, and serverless functions, which is what teams need when they are trying to see which exposures are real. Detection and response can then use threat intelligence and machine learning to surface activity closer to the moment it happens.

CNAPP also supports regulatory work by watching the environment continuously and pointing out where compliance is drifting. For organisations standardising on CrowdStrike, it is a practical way to tighten cloud security without adding another disconnected programme.

posts.title: VMware Discloses Exploitation of Hard-to-Fix vCenter Server Flaw
posts.author: Admin
posts.excerpt: VMware confirmed that a difficult-to-fix vCenter Server vulnerability, first shown at a hacking contest, is being used in live attacks.
paragraphs: A difficult-to-fix vulnerability, first revealed at a Chinese hacking contest five months earlier, is being exploited in the wild, VMware confirmed. The company updated its VMSA-2024-0019 bulletin to acknowledge the live attacks and asked customers to prioritise the available fixes.

For teams running vCenter, the practical step is to identify exposed servers, apply the vendor fix, and watch for signs of misuse while the change rolls out. Fencesense tracks advisories like this so clients can patch what is being used, not only what is newly published.

methodology.text: Structured assessment identifies misconfigurations and weaknesses across applications, infrastructure, and cloud assets.

methodology.title: Penetration Testing & BAS
methodology.text: Manual and automated techniques simulate realistic attack paths while breach and attack simulation validates detective and preventive controls.

methodology.title: Reporting & Remediation
methodology.text: Findings are prioritized by exploitability and business impact, with clear remediation guidance and optional retest to confirm fixes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between penetration testing and breach and attack simulation?
faqs.answer: Penetration testing focuses on finding and exploiting specific weaknesses in a point-in-time assessment. BAS continuously or periodically simulates attack techniques to validate that security controls detect and block threats as expected.

faqs.question: Will testing disrupt production systems?
faqs.answer: We agree rules of engagement and maintenance windows upfront. Intrusive tests use safe techniques where required, and high-risk actions are coordinated with your team.

faqs.question: How often should we run BAS and penetration tests?
faqs.answer: Many regulated and high-risk organizations test at least annually and after major changes. BAS can run more frequently to keep validation aligned with evolving threats.

faqs.question: Do you provide retesting after remediation?
faqs.answer: Yes. Retests confirm that critical findings were fixed effectively and give leadership evidence of closure.

faqs.question: Can testing help with GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS expectations?
faqs.answer: Structured VA/PT and BAS programs support control validation and gap identification that auditors and assessors commonly expect as part of a broader compliance program.

methodology.text: Reporting, tuning, and follow-on work keep the outcome aligned as threats and priorities change.

faqs.question: What data sources do hunts use?
faqs.answer: Endpoint, identity, network, and cloud telemetry you already collect—or we help you onboard gaps.

faqs.question: How is hunting different from monitoring?
faqs.answer: Hunts proactively search for behaviors alerts may miss, based on current adversary activity.

faqs.question: Do you leave behind detections?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sustainable detections and runbooks are a core deliverable.

benefits.title: Incident Investigation

benefits.title: Threat Intelligence Integration
benefits.description: Utilizes global threat databases and AI-driven insights to recognize advanced persistent threats (APTs).

benefits.title: Rapid Response
benefits.description: Incident response capabilities to contain breaches quickly and minimize downtime.
